newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KGHM board, unions dispute in deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Polish KGHM board, unions dispute in deadlock.

text.p: The board and unions at Poland's copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA have reached deadlock in a wages dispute because both sides want to discuss different topics at a potential future meeting.
Seven trade unions at KGHM called on Thursday a strike alert after the firm's management failed to begin talks on pay rise demands and employment guarantees.

"We are ready to sit down and talk with the board any time, but not unless the board agrees to discuss a basic monthly pay rise of 10 percent from April 1 onwards," Jozef Czyczerski, head of the Solidarity union told Reuters.

"We also want the board to agree to discuss a revision of this year's wage indexation of more than 15 percent after the first three quarters and various social guarantees, including 10-year employment guarantees," he said.
The company, one of the world's major copper and silver producers, is slated for privatisation in the second half of this year through flotation on the Warsaw and London bourses.
The unions fear that the sale of the firm would likely entail cuts in the KGHM's current 23,400 jobs.

KGHM's board, however, is not willing to discuss the basic pay rise of 10 percent, saying it would not be legal under the signed collective labour agreements with the unions, which puts the dispute in deadlock, an industry source said.

They source also called the 10-year employment guarantee demand "unrealistic", but said both sides could reach a compromise next week, because a lasting dispute would negatively affect the image of the company before its sale.
The board proposed March 26 as the date for talks but the meeting cannot be arranged until both sides agree on an agenda and it was not immediately clear whether those talks would be held.
